key_insight: Program-as-Weights turns a natural-language task specification into a compact neural artifact that can be reused locally, making fuzzy functions cheap, offline, and reproducible.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical alternative to per-query LLM API use for tasks like log filtering, JSON repair, and ranking, with much lower memory and runtime cost.
method: A 4B compiler converts a natural-language specification into parameter-efficient adapters.
The adapters plug into a frozen 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter that executes the fuzzy function.
The approach is trained and evaluated on FuzzyBench, a released 10M-example dataset.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that a 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter running PAW matches direct prompting of Qwen3-32B while using about one-fiftieth the inference memory and reaching 30 tokens/s on a MacBook M3.
watch_item: The system depends on the quality of compiler-generated adapters and on whether FuzzyBench-style tasks transfer well to unseen fuzzy-function specs.
paper_title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
